fullPassage: Today, commodities for which demand rises as their prices rise are known as Giffen goods. Giffen goods rely on a number of assumptions. First, the commodity has to be an inferior good, that is, a good that people choose to buy less of as their income rises because there are better alternatives; for example, choosing meat over bread. Second, the consumer must spend a large portion of their income on this product, hence the fact that the example refers to the poorest section of society. Finally, there must be no alternatives to the product. In the case of bread, there is no cheaper alternative staple. Given these assumptions, an increase in the price of bread creates two effects. It causes people to buy less bread because the satisfaction it creates per pound of spending falls compared to other goods. This substitution effect would cause bread to follow the general rule of higher price causing lower demand. However, as the price of bread rises, it also reduces the power to spend on other things, and because bread is an inferior good, this lower income will make the demand for bread rise. What makes the Giffen good so special is that because the poor spend so much of their income on bread, the income effect is so large that it outweighs the substitution effect, and so when the price goes up, some people buy more. Another example of a Giffen good is that of potatoes during the Irish Potato Famine of 1845-52, where rising prices allegedly caused an increase in the demand for potatoes.

det.korean: 사람들이 빵을 덜 사게 되는 것은 다른 재화에 비해 만족도가 떨어지기 때문인데, 이 대체효과는 가격이 오르면 수요가 줄어든다는 일반적 법칙을 따르게 만든다. 그러나 소득효과가 이 대체효과를 압도하기 때문에 기펜재 현상이 나타난다.
det.analysis:
① ❌: demand curve는 본문에 언급되지 않은 개념이다.
② ✅: substitution effect — 사람들이 가격 상승으로 다른 재화를 선택하게 되는 현상을 설명하는 부분이며, 뒤에서 소득효과가 이것을 '압도한다(outweighs)'고 대조되므로 두 빈칸 모두 적절하다.
③ ❌: market equilibrium은 본문에 언급되지 않은 개념이다.
④ ❌: income effect는 뒤 문장에서 별도로 설명되는 대조 개념이라 빈칸에 들어갈 수 없다.
det.tip: 같은 단어가 반복되는 빈칸은 앞뒤 문맥에서 대조되는 개념을 구분해야 합니다.

Today, commodities for which demand rises as their prices rise are known as Giffen goods. Giffen goods rely on a number of assumptions.

(A) This substitution effect would cause bread to follow the general rule of higher price causing lower demand. However, as the price of bread rises, it also reduces the power to spend on other things, and because bread is an inferior good, this lower income will make the demand for bread rise.

(B) First, the commodity has to be an inferior good, that is, a good that people choose to buy less of as their income rises because there are better alternatives. Second, the consumer must spend a large portion of their income on this product, hence the fact that the example refers to the poorest section of society. Finally, there must be no alternatives to the product.

(C) In the case of bread, there is no cheaper alternative staple. Given these assumptions, an increase in the price of bread creates two effects. It causes people to buy less bread because the satisfaction it creates per pound of spending falls compared to other goods.

① (A) - (B) - (C)

④ (C) - (B) - (A)
→ (C)의 'Given these assumptions'가 가리킬 가정이 아직 제시되지 않았으므로 도입문 직후에 올 수 없다.
